Import Protein Intensities from a SummarizedExperiment

Source: R/Preprocessing_SE.R
preprocess_se.Rd

Converts a SummarizedExperiment of protein intensities into the proteomics_data object that every NADIA reader returns. It is the way in for data imported with other Bioconductor tools, for instance one of the assays of a QFeatures object. process_proteomics() also accepts the SummarizedExperiment directly and calls this function; call it yourself to keep the object, for example to store it with write_nadia().

Usage

preprocess_se(
  se,
  condition_order = NULL,
  assay_name = NULL,
  log2_input = FALSE,
  condition_column = "Condition",
  replicate_column = "Replicate",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

se

A SummarizedExperiment with protein intensities.

condition_order

Optional character vector with the conditions to keep, in the order they should appear. NULL (default) keeps them all, in the order of the factor levels or, for text, of first appearance.

assay_name

Name or index of the assay with the intensities. NULL (default) takes the first one.

log2_input

TRUE if the intensities are on the log2 scale. Default FALSE, linear intensities.

condition_column

Column of colData(se) with the condition of each sample. Default "Condition".

replicate_column

Column of colData(se) with the replicate number. Default "Replicate"; if the column is absent, the replicates are numbered.

verbose

Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

An object of class c("se_data", "proteomics_data", "list") with the elements metadata, protein_id and protein_quant, like the other readers.

Details

What is read from the object:

  • Intensities: the assay assay_name, proteins in rows and samples in columns. With log2_input = TRUE the values are taken back to the linear scale, because NADIA applies the log2 transformation when it normalises. Zeros are treated as missing values, as for the other readers.

  • Proteins: the row names, which must be present and unique. The gene names come from rowData()$Genes and the descriptions from rowData()$Description, when those columns exist.

  • Design: the condition from colData()[[condition_column]] and the replicate from colData()[[replicate_column]]; without a replicate column the samples are numbered within each condition, in column order.

The samples are renamed <condition>_<replicate>, the convention the rest of NADIA relies on, and the original column names are kept in metadata$R.FileName. Identification metrics (precursor or peptide counts, scores) are not read from rowData(), so those columns of the tables are left empty.

See also

process_proteomics(), which accepts the SummarizedExperiment directly.

Examples

data(nadia_dia)
# A SummarizedExperiment built from the example data
quant <- as.matrix(nadia_dia$protein_quant[, grep("^PG\\.Quantity_",
                                                  names(nadia_dia$protein_quant))])
rownames(quant) <- nadia_dia$protein_quant$PG.ProteinGroups
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
  assays  = list(intensity = quant),
  colData = data.frame(Condition = nadia_dia$metadata$R.Condition,
                       Replicate = nadia_dia$metadata$R.Replicate),
  rowData = data.frame(Genes = nadia_dia$protein_quant$PG.Genes))

pre <- preprocess_se(se, verbose = FALSE)
pre
#> Protein intensities imported from a SummarizedExperiment
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> Samples (metadata): 12 
#> Proteins: 2000 
#> 
#> Conditions: A, B, D 

# The same values on the log2 scale
SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, "intensity") <- log2(quant)
pre_log2 <- preprocess_se(se, log2_input = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
